title: Warn the crossing
location: Pump Room, at the F-1 fire-shutter indicator
script: MARA: Smoke! John, HIT THE STOP!
JOHN: Ivo's under that shutter! It'll trap him!
MARA: Then move him! MOVE!
notes: The possible future shows Ivo beneath or near F-1 while P-1's cabinet smokes. It does not establish that he must be there now. Inspect the warning placard and stop indicator: an E-STOP latches P-1 off and closes **only F-1**. The crew can warn Ivo, isolate power, or route via Lab. Corroboration: John B, Cassidy A, the posted shutter indicator.

title: Stop the pump
script: IVO: John! Wait—I'm at the shutter!
JOHN: It's on FIRE! I'm hitting it!
IVO: Then why's the water still running?!
notes: A future P-1 stop can happen without stopping gravity-fed inflow. This is an **observation**, not evidence that E-STOP failed or software restarted it. F-1 may close; the water-feed question requires examining the header and both branches. Corroboration: Prue A/B, Cassidy B, gallery flow meter.

title: Compare the readings
script: NELL: No. That sensor's wrong. Again.
PRUE: Tank's rising! Feed meter's still moving!
NELL: But Mara shut the intake. I SAW her!
notes: The independent tank-level and common-header flow signals agree. Nell's doubt is credible but not a sensor diagnosis; she watched Mara close CV-1. The closed readout applies only to CV-1, not the whole manifold. Corroboration: Prue B, Cassidy B, Prue A in Act 2; inspect header and both branches.

title: Read the display
script: NELL: Control says CLOSED! That level can't be right!
PRUE: That's just CV-1. What else is there?
NELL: I... don't know. It's still rising!
notes: The readout is accurate for CV-1 but not comprehensive. The exchange identifies CV-1 as the displayed valve but does not establish the other feed or prescribe an operation. Corroboration: Prue A, Cassidy B, Act 2 Prue A/B; the piping diagram is inspectable.

title: Call Loading
script: MARA: Where's Tavi?! Why isn't she answering?!
CASSIDY: Got her! She's in Loading!
MARA: Keep her talking! Don't open that hatch!
notes: Tavi may be alive in Loading, and Mara knows the hatch presents a hazard. This does **not** announce the M-1 crawlway or dictate how to rescue her. Corroboration: John A/B in Act 2, Cassidy A in Act 2, H-1 gauge and station plan.

title: Follow the sound
script: NELL: Hear that ROAR? On Tavi's line?
CASSIDY: She's near a handwheel! Says it's deafening!
NELL: But the intake's shut... isn't it?
notes: The roar suggests water moving near a handwheel in Loading; it does not identify which pipe or where it feeds. Corroboration: Prue A/B, Act 2 Prue A and Cassidy B, local labels/flow indication.

title: Equalize the hatch
location: Tank Gallery, at H-1 pressure hatch
script: TAVI: John! It's at my knees! OPEN IT!
JOHN: Hang on! The pressure's holding it shut!
TAVI: I don't HAVE time!
notes: The future shows a dangerous pressure difference across **H-1**, not the fire shutter. John recognizes pressure against the hatch; the recording does not prescribe how to relieve it. The actual EQ-1 valve and gauge can be examined. M-1 remains a genuine alternative. Corroboration: John B and Cassidy A in Act 2, H-1 placard.

title: Force the hatch
location: Tank Gallery, at H-1 pressure hatch
script: IVO: John, STOP! Hear that water?!
JOHN: Tavi's in there! I'm opening it!
IVO: It'll take you BOTH! JOHN!
notes: A feared surge is a real hazard if H-1 is opened against differential pressure. No recorded outcome or unique preferred intervention follows. The gauge/equalizer and M-1 are discoverable independently. Corroboration: John A, Cassidy A, the hatch pressure indicators.

title: Trace the line
script: IVO: Feel that? This line's LIVE!
PRUE: But CV-1's shut! What the hell?!
IVO: Then we're looking at the wrong one!
notes: The conversation reveals that the live pipe does not match the Control-displayed closed valve. It does **not** name BV-2, its location, or the corrective action. These are established from labels, a line trace, or Ivo when directly questioned. Corroboration: Prue A/B and Cassidy B in Act 1, Cassidy B in Act 2.

title: Keep the supply open
script: MARA: Still rising! Prue, WHERE'S IT COMING FROM?!
PRUE: I found another line! I can't shut it blind!
MARA: FIND IT! We're almost full!
notes: Prue has noticed another line but cannot safely identify its destination from the recording; Mara conveys urgency without giving a valve instruction. Staff, physical labels and inspection determine whether isolation is appropriate. Corroboration: Prue A in Act 2, Cassidy B, Control level/flow indicators.

title: Find another exit
script: TAVI: It's stuck! Water's pushing the hatch!
CASSIDY: Look around! Anything else?!
TAVI: There's something overhead—wait! A hatch!
notes: Tavi notices an overhead hatch, suggesting an alternate way out without proving where it leads. The actual M-1 crawlway is charted on the station map, remains initially reachable, and leads to Dock. If PCs guide Tavi there now, she can leave; no mandatory H-1 puzzle. Corroboration: Cassidy A in Act 1, John A/B in Act 2, map and M-1 hatch.

title: Evacuate before the report
location: Loading, near the manual transfer valve
script: TAVI: Cassidy! Please, it's coming up!
CASSIDY: I've got you! Move! What did you see?!
TAVI: That wheel! By the crates—WIDE OPEN!
notes: Tavi reports an open handwheel near crates, without identifying its function or the full causal path. Players must relate its label and flow indicator to the tank header and CV-1 readout. Corroboration: Cassidy B in Act 1, Prue A/B in Act 2, physical line trace.

title: Lose the pressure trace
script: IVO: We lost the pressure trace! John?!
JOHN: I unplugged it! There's a gauge out there!
IVO: Yeah? Who's watching it?!
notes: Removing the analyzer data link can blank **Control's** live trend while Tank Gallery's mechanical gauge persists. John alludes to an independent gauge, but no monitoring arrangement is established and the tank's physical pressure is unchanged. Corroboration: John B, Prue B, analyzer tag, mechanical gauge.

title: Pull the cart
script: IVO: STOP! The hose is still attached!
JOHN: It's stuck! Help me pull!
IVO: Shit—John! You ripped it loose!
notes: On this bad future branch, moving the cart before disconnecting its **separate sample-water tap** causes a local leak in Lab. The analyzer does not move itself to Gallery and requires no lift. The sample tap and data cable can be handled independently. Corroboration: John A, analyzer label and sample connection in Lab.

title: Find the armed controller
script: MARA: I canceled it! Why's that light on?!
PRUE: Another controller! It's still ARMED!
MARA: Prue... can it restart?
notes: SCH-1 at Control and the physically separate LOC-1 local retry are independent **requests**, not overrides of latched E-STOP or locked motor supply. Prue notices an armed second controller, but Mara cannot tell whether it can restart the motor; inspecting the local schematic reveals actual logic. Corroboration: Prue B, P-1 isolation placard, local lamp and diagram.

title: Cut all power
script: IVO: Everything's dark! What'd you do?!
PRUE: Cut the MAIN! That pump was going to blow!
IVO: And now we're BLIND!
notes: This possible branch illustrates **whole-site** power loss removing Control telemetry; it does not make motor-only breaker isolation impossible. The battery intercom and local mechanical gauge still work. A latched E-STOP or locked-out P-1 breaker safely prevents motor restart. Corroboration: John A, Prue A, power distribution labels, independent gauge.

title: Inspect the relief line
script: NELL: STOP! Don't open that!
CASSIDY: The pipe's split! Where's that pressure go?!
NELL: Not through THERE! It'll burst!
notes: RV-1 is visibly damaged; Cassidy recognizes the split and Nell warns against using it, without establishing how to relieve pressure safely. A stable pressure hold may need no drainage; OUT-1 exists but receiver capacity and path must be checked. Corroboration: Cassidy B, Gallery gauges, labels, pump/feed clues.

title: Question the ordinary outlet
script: NELL: The needle's climbing. Cassidy—LOOK!
CASSIDY: That outlet! Can't we dump it?!
NELL: Into WHAT? Loading's already flooding!
notes: A separate outlet is noticed, but Nell questions where its water would go; actual receiving capacity and destination remain unverified. The station's OUT-1 label, receiver markings and BV-2 conditions supply a sound method. There is no forced need to drain if the tank is safely held. Corroboration: Cassidy A, Prue A/B in Act 2, Loading receiver inspection.
